title: Success indicators of healthcare networks: Synthesis of knowledge and conceptualization of a field-ready quality assessment and management framework
summary:
Health systems today tend to be more fragmented than ever, caused by a lack of coordination or unclear responsibilities, resulting in a decline of care quality. One strategy to counter this fragmentation is the integration of care across sectors and professions. One example of such integrated care are healthcare networks.
To our knowledge, no evidence-based, empirically driven quality assessment tool for healthcare networks has been published that accounts for the structural and functional diversity among them. NetQua's goal is the development of such an instrument using a participatory approach with health networks, umbrella organizations, and patient advocacy groups.
conditions: Quality assessment and management in healthcare networks

interventions.name: This mixed-methods study takes a participatory approach: Key members of staff within participating health networks, umbrella organisations, and patient advocacy groups will give input via focus group interviews, workshops, expert panels, as well as surveys. Data will be collected on past experiences

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sufficient German language skills to participate in expert interviews and surveys, 18 years of age or above. Further criteria depend on the specific survey or interview, e.g., key staff members with expertise in quality assessment within their healthcare network, senior researchers working on related projects within the same funding pool, patient advocacy group members.
Exclusion criteria:
under 18 years of age, insuffcient German language skills
